name: SubMST
description: You are given an undirected unweighted tree $$$T$$$ with $$$n$$$ vertices. Define a complete undirected weighted graph $$$G$$$ with $$$n$$$ vertices, where the weight of the edge between vertices $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ in $$$G$$$ is equal to the distance between the two vertices in the original tree. For every possible subset of vertices, consider the minimum spanning tree (MST) of the subgraph of $$$G$$$ induced by that subset of vertices. Compute the sum of the weights of the MST for all possible subsets of vertices. As this number is big, you are only required to output the sum modulo $$$10^9 + 7$$$.
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10000$$$). The description of the test cases follows. The first line contains an integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \leq n \leq 5000$$$), the number of vertices in the tree. The following $$$n-1$$$ lines contains two integers $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ ($$$1 \leq u,v \leq n$$$), representing an edge between vertices $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ in the tree. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n^2$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$5000^2$$$.
output_specification: Output a single integer, the sum of the MST weights for all possible subsets of vertices, modulo $$$10^9+7$$$.
approach_summary: Precompute 2^k ancestor jumps up[u][k] and node depths in O(N log N). Compute LCA and path aggregates in O(log N) per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2161F — SubMST [146. Binary Lifting and LCA]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary lifting for lowest common ancestor and tree jumps.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Any ancestor jump of distance $K$ can be decomposed into powers of two $K = \sum 2^j$. Precomputing `up[u][k]` (the $2^k$-th ancestor of $u$) via `up[u][k] = up[up[u][k-1]][k-1]` allows any path or LCA to be answered in $O(\log N)$.
